records.title: Soldiers wishing to travel home without authorization
records.header_literal: B) NKJ v LP (06.23 a.m., November 13th); FUER WAU 07.00 2 TLE; 2 TL RICHI-242
records.readable_german: Die Schwierigkeiten, dass Mannschaften eigenmaechtig nach Hause fahren wollen, sind ueberall die gleichen. OHL. RM 1A Nr. 11?01 Geh. Op.
records.meaning: The second part states that the difficulty is the same everywhere: soldiers want to travel home on their own authority. It closes with OHL and an unresolved office reference. It reports the problem; it does not itself authorize those departures.
notes: All 242 printed coordinates are preserved and decode without repairs. The earlier OCR separated the first row and omitted additional source material; those OCR defects are not historical ciphertext losses.

The heading explicitly identifies this as part 2. The independently handled first part has two group-width obliterations and a conditional exclusion model; this native part does not rely on that model.
The literal reference 11?01 retains one globally coupled unknown square cell. No historical file number or date is inferred.

The unknown in 11?01 is the same GA square cell as the first unknown in p186 C1's DRTRM1A?5?; both must have the same unresolved label. The second unknown in that C1 field is AF and must have a different label.

records.title: Baltic transport uncertainty and Graf Goltz preparations
records.header_literal: C) KOW v LP (06.26 a.m., November 13th); 17.40 (13/11) 2 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-182; (Continued)
records.readable_german: Zu DRTRM1A?5?. ABTRSPRT z. Zt. wegen unklarer Lage in Ostsee UNMOGLCH. Gen. Graf Goltz hat jedoch VORBEREITG
records.meaning: This first part concerns transport that is currently described as impossible because the situation in the Baltic Sea is unclear. It then begins a statement about preparations associated with the literal name and title GEN GRAF GOLTZ. The statement is incomplete in this source body, so no completed plan or action is supplied.
notes: All 182 source slots are preserved. Source index 110 has an F/R-like shape with an attached lower-right diagonal and is masked as ?; the unchanged edited reading supplies F there, producing the E in GEN at plaintext index 61. This is one source-mask fill, not an observed coordinate or a repair-cost reduction. The scan labels two parts and prints “Continued,” but only this first body is included here.

DRTRM1A?5?, ABTRSPRT, UNMOGLCH and VORBEREITG are retained literally. The English meaning interprets the abbreviated transport statement; no missing I, vowel or grammatical ending is added to the decoded stream.
The two question marks in the opening reference come from different unresolved square cells; their labels remain globally injective rather than being independently guessed.
The literal name GRAF GOLTZ is not used to add a first name or identify a historical biography.

The former F interpretation is retained as an explicit sensitivity assumption: it gives 89 fixed raw positions and no coordinate changes. The conservative source edition has 88 fixed raw positions and one fill; no new key assignment or independent coordinate witness is claimed.
